native_result.HypoB: In this NLS sample (N = 8,773), the effect of a respondent's socioeconomic status (SES) on the probability of completing a bachelor's degree, which is positive and strongly significant in the baseline model containing only social-background controls (race, sex, family size), collapses to a statistically insignificant and marginally negative value once the model additionally adjusts for academic characteristics (ASVAB composite and high-school class percentile) together with race. SES is the only candidate among {SES, sex_Male, family size} whose coefficient matches this sign-and-significance flip; the male dummy is already insignificant in baseline (no flip), and family size remains significantly negative throughout. The pattern is the textbook mediation-by-mediators result: SES's bivariate effect on BA completion is absorbed by (i) racial disparities in BA completion and (ii) academic preparedness (ASVAB scores, class rank), both of which are themselves strongly correlated with SES.
